panic.title: Stop everything?
panic.body: Kills {sessions, plural, one {# session} other {# sessions}}, pauses {schedules, plural, one {# schedule} other {# schedules}}, disconnects {channels, plural, one {# channel} other {# channels}}, and tells {clouds, plural, =0 {no cloud daemons} one {# cloud daemon} other {# cloud daemons}} to do the same. Nothing restarts until you resume.
panic.resumeBody: Check what was running before you bring it back.
panic.resumeN: {count, plural, =0 {Resume without agents} one {Resume # selected} other {Resume # selected}}
offline.banner: Offline. Showing what was cached. Approvals you make now are sent when you're back online.
demo.banner: Demo data. Nothing here is connected to a real daemon.
update.ready: A new version of beamhop is ready.
channels.pair.confirmHint: Check this is your account. If someone else used the code first, unpair them and get a new code.
channels.pair.unpairedSpoken: Unpaired. A new code is ready.
channels.pair.qrLabel: QR code that opens {bot} in Telegram
channels.pair.qrHint: Telegram on your phone? Scan this with the camera. It opens the bot and pairs you in one tap.
channels.pair.orSend: Or send this to the bot:
channels.pair.send.slack: In Slack, send this to {bot} in a DM:
channels.pair.send.discord: Send this in any channel {bot} can see, or in a DM:
channels.pair.expired: This code expired. Codes last 10 minutes and work once.
channels.pair.safety: Whoever sends this code first becomes an owner of this channel. Don't share it.
channels.add.title: Add a channel
channels.wizard.title: Add {provider}
channels.wizard.doneToast: {provider} is connected. Your agents can be reached there now.
channels.wizard.generic: This step is provided by a channel plugin. Finish it in the terminal for now.
channels.wizard.goneBody: It was removed while this setup was open. Start over to add it again.
channels.wizard.saved: Progress is saved. Tokens are not — they go straight to the keychain.
channels.wizard.resumed: Picked up where you left off with {name}.
channels.create.tg.title: Create a bot with @BotFather
channels.create.tg.lead: BotFather is Telegram's own bot for making bots. It takes about a minute; come back here with the token.
channels.create.tg.s2note: Shown in chats. You can change it later with /setname.
channels.create.tg.s3note: 5–32 characters, ends in bot, can't be changed later. Taken? Change the middle letters.
channels.create.tg.s4: BotFather replies with a token. Copy it and come back here.
channels.create.sl.title: Create the Slack app from a manifest
channels.create.sl.lead: The link opens Slack with name, scopes, events, Socket Mode and /pair already filled in. Nothing to configure by hand.
channels.create.sl.appNameHint: How the app appears in your workspace.
channels.create.sl.s1: Pick your workspace, review the summary, then press Create.
channels.create.sl.s2: Stay on the app's page: the next step needs two tokens from it.
channels.create.dc.title: Create a Discord application
channels.create.dc.lead: Do these four things in the Developer Portal. Tick them off as you go — the list is for you, it isn't checked.
channels.create.dc.app: New Application · give it a name
channels.create.dc.intentWhy: Needed so the agent can read messages that mention it.
channels.create.dc.note: Discord shows the token once. If you lose it, reset it again — the old one stops working.
channels.cred.lead.one: beamhop checks its shape first, then asks the provider who the bot is. The token goes to your OS keychain, never into a config file.
channels.cred.lead.slack: Slack uses one token to connect (Socket Mode) and one to post. Both go to your OS keychain.
channels.cred.savedLead: The token is in your keychain. To change it later, use Replace token on the channel.
channels.cred.how.telegram.bot-token: From BotFather's reply after /newbot. Lost it? Send /token to BotFather.
channels.cred.how.slack.app-token: Basic Information → App-Level Tokens → Generate, with scope connections:write.
channels.cred.how.slack.bot-token: Install App → Install to Workspace → copy the Bot User OAuth Token.
channels.cred.how.nostr.nsec: Only if the group needs its own key.
channels.cred.welcomeBack: Back? Paste the {label} you just copied.
channels.cred.name: Channel name
channels.cred.nameHint: Used in the CLI and in routes, like {name}:dm.
channels.cred.nameRule: Use lowercase letters, digits and dashes.
channels.pairStep.title: Link your {provider} account as owner
channels.pairStep.lead: So {bot} knows who you are: owners can approve, stop and reconfigure agents from {provider}.
channels.join.title: Choose who answers here
channels.join.lead: Pick the agents {bot} speaks for, where they listen, and what new people can do.
channels.join.noAgents: No agents yet. You can join agents to this channel later from Agents.
channels.join.inChannels: {count, plural, =0 {in no channels yet} one {in # channel} other {in # channels}}
channels.join.dmsHint: People who DM {bot} reach the agent.
channels.join.tg.waitingGroup: Groups appear here once the bot is added…
channels.join.tg.privacy: Should the agent read every message, not only mentions? Send /setprivacy to @BotFather → Disable. Then remove and re-add the bot to the group — Telegram only applies it on re-join.
channels.join.sl.invite: To add it to a Slack channel, send this in that channel:
channels.join.dc.noClient: Couldn't read the application id from the token. Use OAuth2 → URL Generator in the portal instead.
channels.join.dc.perms: Asks for the minimum: view channels, send messages, embed links, attach files, read message history.
channels.join.dc.threadsHint: Adds the Send Messages in Threads permission.
channels.join.role: Default role for people the agent doesn't know yet
channels.join.done: {agents} joined · {count, plural, one {# place} other {# places}}
channels.nostr.relayLead: NIP-29 groups live on one relay that enforces membership. beamhop checks it supports groups (NIP-11) before you continue.
channels.nostr.relayHint: wss:// only. Paste the address the group admin shared.
channels.nostr.keyDaemonHint: Recommended. Each agent already has a Nostr identity in your keychain.
channels.nostr.keyOwnHint: For groups that admitted a specific npub.
channels.nostr.nsecHint: Held in memory until you connect, then saved to the keychain.
channels.nostr.groupLead: The group id on {relay}. You can paste the whole address (host'group).
channels.add.lead: Connect a place where people can reach your agents. Credentials go to your OS keychain; you never edit a config file.
channels.add.errorBody: Showing the built-in providers. Plugin channels appear once the daemon answers.
channels.add.pluginBody: Matrix, Signal, email… install a channel plugin from the CLI and it shows up here.
channels.list.nostrGroups: {count, plural, =0 {no groups} one {# group (NIP-29)} other {# groups (NIP-29)}}
channels.list.agents: {count, plural, =0 {no agents} one {# agent} other {# agents}}
channels.list.slugAttention: {count, plural, one {# needs you} other {# need you}}
channels.list.errorBody: The daemon didn't answer. Your channels keep running; this only affects what you see here.
channels.list.emptyBody: Connect Telegram, Slack or Discord so people can reach your agents there. Nostr DMs already work.
channels.detail.notFoundBody: It may have been removed from another device or the CLI.
channels.detail.errorBody.telegram: Telegram stopped accepting the bot token — usually because it was revoked in @BotFather. Replace it; memberships and pairings stay.
channels.detail.errorBody.slack: Slack stopped accepting a token. Reinstalling the app or rotating tokens does this. Replace them; everything else stays.
channels.detail.errorBody.other: The provider stopped accepting the token. Replace it; memberships and pairings stay. beamhop retries every 30 s until then.
channels.detail.keychain: {count, plural, one {# secret in keychain} other {# secrets in keychain}}
channels.detail.noOwners: No {provider} account is paired as owner yet. Pair yours to approve and stop agents from {provider}.
channels.detail.noMembers: No agent listens on this channel yet. Join one from its Agent page → Memberships.
channels.detail.removeBody: {count, plural, =0 {No agent listens here.} one {# agent stops listening here.} other {# agents stop listening here.}} The token is deleted from your keychain and pairings are forgotten. The bot itself stays on {provider} — delete it there if you don't need it.
channels.detail.replaceBody: Paste the new token. beamhop checks it with the provider before saving; memberships, pairings and routes stay as they are.
